source_title: TT Electronics Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 55 and 115 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 3 March 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 11% to £478.2m, including 4% organic growth, underlying operating profit 20% to £40.0m and underlying operating margin 60bps to 8.4%. Operating cash flow rose 43% to £35.9m, cash conversion reached 98% and free cash flow increased 14% to £9.7m. Net debt rose to £69.1m following acquisitions and investment, but leverage remained within the target range and the pension scheme was fully funded on an actuarial basis.
already_announced_exclusion: The announced self-help programme, footprint and fixed-cost initiatives, completed acquisition integrations and associated restructuring costs disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Broad-based growth, margin expansion, excellent cash conversion and strong operating cash flow provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence. Acquisition-related debt growth creates only limited pressure.

source_title: TT Electronics Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 77 and 139 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 8 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 10% organically to £476.2m, adjusted operating profit 27% to £34.8m and adjusted margin 90bps to 7.3%, with statutory profit also improving and a record order book. Supply-chain constraints and inventory investment reduced cash conversion to 65%, while net debt rose to £102.5m and leverage to 1.7x. Nonetheless, leverage remained within the 1-2x target, interest cover was 13.5x and available facilities totalled £272.4m.
already_announced_exclusion: The announced self-help footprint programme, completed Barbados, Carrollton and Corpus Christi closures, Plano move, Torotel and power-supply integrations and other disclosed operational-efficiency actions are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Supply-chain constraints, lower cash conversion, inventory absorption and higher debt create moderate cash pressure. Strong organic growth, margin expansion, record demand, low leverage and ample liquidity provide very strong offsets.

source_title: TT Electronics Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 69 and 129 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 6 March 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue was broadly stable at £613.9m and rose 1% organically, while adjusted operating profit increased 12% to £52.8m and adjusted margin 100bps to 8.6%. Cash conversion recovered from 33% to 92%, free cash flow reversed from a £13.1m outflow to a £23.9m inflow, net debt fell to £126.2m and leverage improved to 1.7x. Statutory profit was constrained by a £32.5m non-cash write-down on businesses already held for sale and disclosed restructuring costs.
already_announced_exclusion: The announced sale of the Cardiff, Hartlepool and Dongguan units, Project Albert write-down, Covina-to-Kansas relocation, Ferranti and Torotel integration, pension restructuring and final self-help programme actions are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Strong adjusted profit and margin growth, restored cash conversion, positive free cash flow and falling debt and leverage provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence. Flat headline revenue and already-announced portfolio actions create little additional forward pressure.
